# At a glance

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Format | Standard (Reality Fracture, set code `fra`, plus Standard mana support) |
| Colors | Red, green, white (Naya) |
| Archetype | Prepared-artifact combo, aggressive midrange shell |
| Size | 60 cards, 24 lands, 36 spells |
| Primary win | Craterclaw Colossus: a board of Heartwood tokens turns its enters trigger into trample plus a team-wide power spike |
| Secondary win | Aerid Konstrari grows by the number of artifacts you control; Hall of Echoes copies it for a second flier |
| Land as engine | Hall of Echoes copies the biggest creature for {5}; Restless Ridgeline is a 3/4 attacker that pumps and untaps a friend |

# Overview

Every creature in the engine is a spell in disguise. The Reality Fracture prepared creatures — Heartwood Crafter,
Konstrari Improviser, Woodwork Prodigy and Blossom-Blessed Angel — enter the battlefield prepared, which means the
sorcery printed on their back face can be cast once for free. This deck's back face is **Soul Tether**, a
`{2}{R/G}` sorcery that makes a Heartwood token: a red and green artifact with `{T}: Add {R} or {G}`.

That single loop supplies everything the deck wants. Heartwood tokens are mana, so the deck reaches five, six and
seven mana without playing a ramp spell. They are also artifacts, which is the number Craterclaw Colossus reads, and
the number Aerid Konstrari reads. Twelve creatures produce tokens, so the artifact count climbs on its own:
Woodwork Prodigy re-prepares during your upkeep, which means one free Heartwood every turn from a single three-drop.

The white half is small and load-bearing. Blossom-Blessed Angel is the second prepared body — a 2/4 flier with
vigilance that hands out a free +1/+1 counter and a life — and the equipment in the list is both a real pump and
artifact padding for the two payoff creatures.

Nothing here is a fragile two-card combo: every piece advances the artifact count itself, so answering one creature
slows the engine rather than stopping it.

# Approach

## Game plan phases

| Phase | Turns | What you are doing |
|---|---|---|
| Setup | 1–2 | Heartwood Crafter or Marwyn on one, Konstrari Improviser on two. Cast the free Soul Tether the turn the body lands |
| Build | 3–4 | Woodwork Prodigy, then Traxos or Aerid Konstrari. Every upkeep adds another Heartwood |
| Conversion | 5–6 | Craterclaw Colossus: by now the artifact count is five to eight, so the team attacks for lethal |
| Close | 6+ | Hall of Echoes copies Aerid or Craterclaw; Restless Ridgeline finishes through a stall |

## Curve and mana

| Mana value | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 7 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cards | 9 | 12 | 4 | 8 | 3 |

Twenty-four lands, nine one-drops and twelve two-drops: the deck almost always has a play on turn one and two, which
is what keeps the goldfish consistency at 0.638 and P(four lands by turn four) at 0.623. Craterclaw Colossus is listed
at seven, but Heartwood tokens mean it usually lands on turn five. The functional average is under three.

# Gameplay strategy

## Early game

Lead with a prepared body, not with equipment. Heartwood Crafter on one is the ideal curve: it enters prepared, so
turn one is a 1/1 plus a Heartwood token, and from then on every Soul Tether copy is a free mana rock. Its own
`{T}: Add {C}` cannot pay for spells cast from your hand, so treat that ability as a bonus rather than a plan.

Konstrari Improviser on two is the stronger clock — a 2/2 plus a token. Hold Woodwork Prodigy until you can protect
it; it is the only repeatable token source and opponents will point removal at it. Do not trade Heartwood tokens for
damage early: they are the mana that casts Craterclaw, and they are the number Craterclaw and Aerid read.

## The combo turn

The kill is a mass pump, not an infinite loop:

1. Untap with five or more artifacts on the battlefield — in practice three Heartwoods plus an equipment and a body.
2. Cast Craterclaw Colossus for `{4}{R}{R}{R}`. Its trigger counts artifacts you control as it resolves, itself included.
3. The whole team gains trample and gets +X/+0. With six artifacts that is a 5/5 haste trampler plus every other
   creature swinging for six more than printed.
4. Konstrari Charm's second mode adds two counters and trample to whichever creature is being chump-blocked.

Against a board stall, add Hall of Echoes: for {5} the land becomes a second Craterclaw, which fires the pump trigger
again and stacks a second trample bonus on the same attack.

## Win condition 2 — Aerid Konstrari and the manland

Aerid Konstrari is a 4/4 flier for four that makes a Heartwood when it enters and another when it dies, and its
{6} ability converts the artifact count into power. With six artifacts it attacks as a 10/4 flier, which races any
ground deck. Hall of Echoes copying Aerid is the cleanest finisher in the deck: the copy is a land until end of turn,
so sorcery-speed creature removal does not answer it.

Restless Ridgeline is the third route. Three mana turns it into a 3/4, and each attack gives another attacker +2/+0
and untaps it — a loop of small advantages that closes games where the big creatures were answered.

## Mulligan guide

| Hand | Keep? | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Two lands, Heartwood Crafter, Konstrari Improviser | Yes | The engine starts on turn one and the tokens fix the rest |
| One land, one one-drop, one two-drop | Yes on the play | Nine one-drops make this a real hand |
| Five lands, one payoff, no engine | No | The payoffs read a count that nothing is building |
| Craterclaw plus two equipment, no creatures | No | Equipment without bodies is just artifacts and no clock |
| Woodwork Prodigy, three lands, Konstrari Charm | Yes | Prodigy alone produces a token every turn from turn four |

## Key interactions and edge cases

- **Prepared is one-shot per preparation.** Casting the Soul Tether copy unprepares the creature. Only Woodwork
  Prodigy re-arms itself, and only during your upkeep, so a Prodigy killed at sorcery speed costs you the future
  tokens, not just the body.
- **Craterclaw counts artifacts as it resolves.** Sacrificing a Heartwood to Marwyn in response lowers X, so make
  the draw decision before combat, not during it.
- **Aerid Konstrari's pump is a one-shot.** The +X/+0 lasts until end of turn; the Heartwood it makes does not.
- **Traxos, Scourge Eternal does not untap on its own.** It untaps when you cast an artifact or creature spell, so a
  turn with only Konstrari Charm leaves it tapped on defence.
- **Solitary Cell is an artifact first.** It exiles a permanent with mana value three or less until it leaves, so
  destroying your own Cell returns their permanent — and it counts for Craterclaw while it sits there.
- **Restless Ridgeline enters tapped.** Do not count it as a turn-one red source; lead on Stomping Ground when you need
  red immediately.

## Matchups

| Opponent | Plan |
|---|---|
| Aggro | Trade early with Konstrari Charm and Solitary Cell, then land Blossom-Blessed Angel as a blocker that also grows. The deck wants the game to reach turn five |
| Control | Hold Woodwork Prodigy until they tap out, and keep a second prepared body in hand. Hall of Echoes and Restless Ridgeline dodge sorcery-speed sweepers |
| Midrange | Race with Aerid plus tokens; their removal is one-for-one against a deck that rebuilds the count every turn |
| Combo | No countermagic, so the plan is speed: tokens on turns one and two, Craterclaw on five, and Konstrari Charm's six damage for a key flier |
